headline: Approved a written request asking Parks and Rec to install a sign like other town parks.
summary: The group also discussed e-bike rules and trail signs in the park. A financial report showed a combined total of $32,894.34, and a resident asked whether the trail could extend north or south. The meeting also noted the death of committee member Bob Kennedy.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 1, 2026 meeting.
Approved a motion asking Wallingford Parks and Rec, in a written letter, to install a park sign consistent with other town parks.

Item 1: Call To Order   
The QRLTAC was called to order by Co-chair Cathy Granucci at 7:05 pm.  
 
Item 2: Attendance 
Cathy Granucci, Co-chair 
Mary Mushinsky, Co-chair

Item 3: Approve & Accept Minutes from October 1, 2026 
Motion: Robin Corrigan; Seconded: Sally Tremaine; Motion: Passed 
 
Item 4: Co-Chair Announcements  
Committee member Bob Kennedy passed away last night after a decline in health. 
 
Holiday on the Trail is Sunday, November 29. We have in place the Amphenol parking lot, a police 
oƯicer to direct traƯic, Allyn Miller’s Double M Ranch horse carriage rental ($1,500 + $50 for fuel). 
Cathy asked Walmart for three $50 gift cards to buy cookies, a tree, etc. High schools and town 
Social Services were notiﬁed about our need for volunteers. SCOW teen chorus can perform for a 
$150 donation. Kenny Marshall can provide cocoa for $300. We will display our ZeƯy donation ﬂyer. 
We need a Santa actor, and we need a DJ with music system. 
 
The Festival of Trees raƯle is during the Holiday Stroll on Friday, December 4; we need gift cards to 
include in the raƯle. 
 
Cathy will host a holiday party at her house on Thursday, December 3. 
 
On November 16, 3:00 at town hall, the engineering company will present their design for the new 
Yalesville entrance to Fireworks Island. 
 
We received a complaint about a homeless man camping in the woods with an aggressive dog on 
the trail. Cathy had the police investigate. The dog is gone, and the police are aware of the situation.
We had a discussion of e-bike policy and trail rules signage in the park. 
 
Item 5: Town Engineer Report 
None. 
 
Item 6: Sub-committee Reports  
1. Financial Report: Robin Corrigan 
Operating (checking):  $  2,938.78 
Money Market:   $  1,346.75 
Savings (7-month CD): $11,108.81 
Nonproﬁt checking:  $17,500.00 (donation from Amphenol) 
Combined:   $32,894.34 
2. Grants/Applications: Mary Mushinsky 
 Wallingford did not get a grant for trail extensions; but the legislature passed another trail 
grant fund in May. Mary is working to get funding through the Urban Act. 
 
3. Publicity/Social Media: Sally Tremaine, Jay Cosgrove 
The announcement of the Yalesville house demolition created a surge of activity on our 
Facebook page. 
4. Signage: Sheila Dravis Cosgrove, Jay Cosgrove, Tom Knight, Melissa Hasselbarth 
Sheila recommends that the town install a sign similar to other town parks. (See motion 
below) 
5. Trail Expansion: Fred Nellums, Tom Knight, David Bedell 
None. 
 
Item 7: Public Q & A  
Jessica Wysocki spoke about the blue trail system including the trail through Quinnipiac River State 
Park, and the potential for our trail to extend south or north. Mary explained why the old trail was 
abandoned due to ﬂooding, and her investigation into a potential trail on either the river’s east side 
(Valley Service Road) or west side (Wilbur Cross Parkway). 
 
Item 8: Other Business  
Sheila Dravis moved to ask Wallingford Parks and Rec, in a written letter, to install a sign consistent 
with other town parks: “Welcome to ____ Park”; “Please Note”; “Parks and Park Facilities Code” . 
David Bedell seconded; motion passed. 
 
Item 9: Next Regular Meeting: January 7, 2026 
 
Item 10: Adjournment  
The QRLTAC adjourned at 8:32 PM.
